title: Acute lower GI bleeding
subject: gastroenterology
setting: Emergency department, ward, endoscopy and interventional radiology
summary: Classify by shock index; unstable patients (shock index above 1) get CT angiography then embolisation, stable patients are scored with Oakland (8 or less: outpatient investigation). Transfuse restrictively and perform non-urgent inpatient colonoscopy for major bleeds.

sections.title: Recognise and stratify
items: Fresh or maroon blood per rectum. Common causes: diverticular bleeding, angioectasia, ischaemic, infective or inflammatory colitis, post-polypectomy bleeding, haemorrhoids, neoplasia. In India also consider intestinal tuberculosis, amoebic or bacillary colitis and solitary rectal ulcer.
Shock index (heart rate divided by systolic BP) above 1 after initial resuscitation = unstable bleed (BSG 2019).

Stable patients: calculate the Oakland score. 8 points or less with no other reason for admission = minor bleed, suitable for discharge and urgent outpatient colonoscopy. Above 8 = major bleed, admit.

Oakland points (1 of 2): age below 40 = 0, 40 to 69 = 1, 70 or more = 2; male = 1; previous LGIB admission = 1; blood on rectal examination = 1; heart rate below 70 = 0, 70 to 89 = 1, 90 to 109 = 2, 110 or more = 3.

Oakland points (2 of 2): systolic BP below 90 = 5, 90 to 119 = 4, 120 to 129 = 3, 130 to 159 = 2, 160 or more = 0; Hb (g/L) below 70 = 22, 70 to 89 = 17, 90 to 109 = 13, 110 to 129 = 8, 130 to 159 = 4, 160 or more = 0.
Suspect an upper GI source in brisk haematochezia with instability, especially with a BUN to creatinine ratio above 30 (both in mg/dL), peptic ulcer history, NSAID use or portal hypertension.

sections.title: Resuscitation and antithrombotics
items: Two large-bore cannulae, crystalloid resuscitation, group and crossmatch.

Transfuse red cells at Hb below 7 g/dL (70 g/L), target 7 to 9 g/dL after transfusion. With cardiovascular disease use a trigger of 8 g/dL and target 10 g/dL (BSG 2019); ACG 2023 accepts 8 g/dL in cardiovascular disease or acute coronary syndrome.
Warfarin: stop at presentation; if unstable reverse with prothrombin complex concentrate and vitamin K. Endoscopic therapy is considered safe with INR below 2.5 (ACG 2023).

DOAC: stop at presentation. Reserve specific reversal (idarucizumab for dabigatran; andexanet for factor Xa inhibitors) for life-threatening bleeding not responding to resuscitation and drug cessation.
Tranexamic acid is not recommended in lower GI bleeding (ACG 2023; BSG: trials only).

Aspirin for primary prevention: stop permanently. Aspirin for secondary prevention: do not stop routinely. Dual antiplatelet therapy with coronary stents: continue aspirin, discuss the P2Y12 inhibitor with cardiology and restart it within 5 days.

sections.title: Localise the bleeding
items: Bloods: CBC, urea, creatinine, electrolytes, LFT, coagulation profile, group and crossmatch.
Unstable (shock index above 1) or suspected active bleeding: CT angiography first; it is fast, needs no bowel preparation and images the whole GI tract.

Positive CTA: catheter angiography with embolisation as soon as possible; within 60 minutes for unstable patients in centres with 24/7 interventional radiology (BSG). Colonoscopy is an alternative for a colonic source (ACG).
Unstable with a negative CTA: upper GI endoscopy immediately. If the patient stabilises after resuscitation, gastroscopy may be the first test.
Stable major bleed: inpatient colonoscopy on the next available list after adequate bowel preparation. Urgent colonoscopy within 24 hours has not improved outcomes (ACG 2023).
Colonoscopy may not be needed if bleeding has stopped and a good-quality colonoscopy within the past 12 months showed diverticulosis without neoplasia (ACG 2023).

sections.title: Haemostasis
items: Bowel preparation for urgent colonoscopy: polyethylene glycol electrolyte solution 4 to 6 L over 3 to 4 hours, via nasogastric tube if needed. Distal known source (for example post-polypectomy): enema and washing may suffice.
Diverticular bleeding with stigmata: through-the-scope clips placed on the vessel, endoscopic band ligation or coagulation.
Angioectasia: argon plasma coagulation. Post-polypectomy bleeding: clips or other endoscopic therapy.
Rebleeding after initial control: repeat colonoscopy or CTA depending on stability.
Surgery only after every effort to localise the bleeding by radiology or endoscopy, except in exceptional circumstances.

sections.title: Discharge and restarting drugs
items: Minor bleed (Oakland 8 or less, no other reason to admit): discharge with urgent outpatient colonoscopy.
Stop non-aspirin NSAIDs after diverticular bleeding.

Warfarin, low thrombotic risk: restart at 7 days. High thrombotic risk (mechanical mitral valve, AF with prosthetic valve or mitral stenosis, VTE within 3 months): consider LMWH from 48 hours after the bleed (BSG).
DOAC: restart within a maximum of 7 days after haemorrhage once haemostasis is secure.

sections.title: Pitfalls
items: Missing an upper GI source in the shocked patient with haematochezia.
Sending an unstable patient for unprepared colonoscopy instead of CT angiography.
Blind laparotomy without localisation.
Over-transfusion, and not restarting secondary-prevention aspirin or anticoagulation.

drugs.name: Packed red cells
drugs.dose: Transfuse at Hb below 7 g/dL (below 8 g/dL with cardiovascular disease)
drugs.notes: Target 7 to 9 g/dL after transfusion; 10 g/dL with cardiovascular disease (BSG).

drugs.name: Idarucizumab
drugs.notes: Dabigatran reversal for life-threatening bleeding only.

drugs.name: Polyethylene glycol electrolyte solution
drugs.dose: 4 to 6 L orally or by nasogastric tube over 3 to 4 hours
drugs.notes: Rapid purge before urgent inpatient colonoscopy.
